parsed.explanation: The combined regime rests on a criminal statute on same-sex conduct that applies to a trans visitor travelling in a same-sex relationship, with no documented enforcement against trans visitors. There is no documented trans-specific entry, document or screening rule, and no legal gender recognition, which is a resident gap and not deducted. Institutional hostility is documented: registrars and the commerce ministry have refused LGBTI organisations, officials have criticised same-sex conduct, and an absolute monarchy punishes dissent harshly. Healthcare discrimination figures are 2019 and LGBTQ-wide, and the two killings are 2015 or earlier individual incidents with no rate. Positives include a police-escorted Pride in 2018 and inclusive HIV and family-planning policy, but no documented operative trans protection. Recourse is thin and the 2023 court ruling has not produced registration.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry or document rule documented. Home passport read as issued with no administrative alignment route; mismatch handling at border not sourced.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry could lead to questioning, but how officials treat it is unresolved.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Criminal law on same-sex conduct applies to a trans visitor in a same-sex relationship. No documented arrests, detention or custody practice targeting trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Partner travel is the main pathway into the criminal statute; detention conditions and custody placement are not sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility or bathroom rule. Official and religious hostility recorded, but no state facility policy.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not applicable on this record; no sub-national regimes documented.

care_services.exposure: 2019 survey: 59% of LGBTQ respondents reported discriminatory or disrespectful treatment at public health facilities and 30% were denied services. Not trans-specific and dated.
care_services.protection: 2013 policy requires family-planning and HIV services regardless of sexual orientation, and 2012 HIV outreach was extended to same-sex couples.
care_services.interaction: Policy is inclusive, but practice documented as refusal-prone; the gap is unmeasured after 2019.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials have criticised same-sex conduct as not part of local custom. A minister dismissed UN calls for protection. Registrars refused LGBTI groups on morality grounds, and the commerce ministry still refuses registration in 2026.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Broadcasting guidelines bar content inciting hatred on sexual orientation. A 2023 supreme court ruling declared a registrar decision void.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing is hostile to organising, but the rule of law partly checks it; the refusal persists despite the ruling.

minors_guardians.exposure: Same-sex couples cannot adopt, so a trans visitor travelling with a minor in a same-sex partnership has no recognised guardian status. Trans-specific minor-related rules are not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel with a same-sex partner increases exposure to the criminal statute and to lack of recognised parental standing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two individual killings of a lesbian woman (2015) and a gay man (earlier). No trans-specific violence rate or general homicide baseline. Religious hate speech by pastors recorded in 2018.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police-escorted Pride (2018) and virtual Pride (2021) passed without incident. National guidelines name LGBT people as higher-risk for gender-based violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police role in protecting LGBTI gatherings is documented positively but not for individual trans victims; recent violence is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory discrimination remedy. LGBTI organisations cannot register, so no advocacy channel exists for a visitor. Civic space is closed generally.
remedies_unknowns.protection: High Court 2022 and supreme court 2023 rulings recognised constitutional rights to association, privacy and expression, but registration still refused.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin recourse; the court's reasoning is not shown to have changed practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a documented universal entry ban and exclusion regime for trans visitors. This dossier documents no entry ban or trans-specific border rule, so it sits above 0.35-A. Its criminal statute on same-sex conduct is a latent exposure, not a routine trans-specific exclusion.

0.45-B documents bureaucratic denial of gender-related care and enrolment for nonresidents by rule. Here care refusal is documented only as a 2019 LGBTQ-wide survey figure with no current rule, so this case is somewhat higher than 0.45-B.

0.25-D documents police entrapment and blackmail of trans people under a vice statute. This dossier documents no police targeting of trans people, so it sits above 0.25-D, though the criminal statute and the absence of recourse keep it below the 0.55 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The criminal statute on same-sex conduct reaches a trans visitor only through a same-sex partnership, and no enforcement against trans people is documented. Hostility is mainly official and institutional, through refused LGBTI registration, official criticism and an absolute monarchy that punishes dissent. The most concrete visitor-facing risk is care refusal, but that evidence is LGBTQ-wide and dated to 2019. The two killings are old individual incidents with no rate. Absent recourse and the lack of documented trans-specific border or facility rules keep the rating in the elevated band, but unresolved document questions and the statute prevent a higher score.
